app.title: What does love sound like?
app.sub: Design a small experiment. Hear the answer. Share it.
i18n.review: This translation is a draft awaiting review.
age.note: Either answer is fine. If you'd rather not say, open research and putting your own words in links stay off.
home.example.t: A film's love theme → its chords → the feelings in them → notes → your sound.
home.empty.mine: Nothing yet. Your first experiment takes about a minute.
home.empty.shared: When someone sends you an experiment, it lands here.
prog.streak0: Discover something today to start a streak
prog.alphabet: You've found the whole alphabet of love.
stage.question: Question
q.film: What does a film's love sound like?
q.someone: What does someone I love sound like?
q.culture: What does love sound like where I'm from?
question.lead: Every experiment starts with a question.
size.big: Big — every stage, up to three sources
source.lead: Where does the inspiration come from?
source.text: Name it in a few words
source.text.hint: Stays on this device unless you choose to put it in a link.
chords.fromletters: Built from your feelings' home chords.
chords.note: Chords only — never the tune, never the words.
chords.tap: Tap a chord to hear it.
emotions.guess: The studio's first guess is glowing — you decide.
notes.note: The studio's own pattern over the harmony, shaped by your feelings — not the melody of any work.
notes.relove: ends with love called and answered: D → G
sound.relove: End with love called and answered (D → G)
sound.locked: More voices and tenses unlock after {n} discoveries.
result.echo: A different colour to try next
result.echo.t: Your sound leans {a}. Try {b} next — it sits on the other side of the alphabet.
found.harmony: a harmony you had not heard
result.saved: Saved to your notebook on this device.
card.why: Harmony credited to {attr}. Feelings chosen by the person who made it; the studio only guessed first.
card.why.personal: Inspired by {sources}. Feelings chosen by the person who made it.
share.pub: Put the words I typed into the link
share.pub.blocked: Links, emails, handles and phone numbers are never put into a link.
share.text: I made mine. Make yours, or remix it.
share.private: Your typed words stay on this device; the link says only “{kind}”.
shared.bad: This link didn't open. It may have been cut short.
notebook.title: Notebook
knows.local.items: your experiments, what you have unlocked, your language, and your answer to the age question.
knows.sent.none: Nothing, unless you say yes to open research below.
knows.links: A share link carries the experiment inside the link itself, after the “#”. Browsers do not send that part to any server.
knows.research.t: You can add an experiment to an open, public dataset about how love sounds across cultures. You see exactly what would be sent before anything is.
knows.clear: Start over — erase everything this page kept
research.offer: Add this to the open research?
research.what: Exactly this would be sent — nothing else:
research.closed: The research round for the studio isn't open yet. Nothing was sent.
research.failed: It could not be sent. Nothing was stored elsewhere.
research.age: Open research is for people 13 or older.
tpl.title: Experiments
tpl.sub: A hundred ways to ask one question. Start with any open one.
tpl.own.sub: Pick any source and build the stages yourself.
tpl.english: Experiment texts are in English for now.
api.title: Add this to the open dataset?
api.copy: Add my experiment to the free, open dataset of what love sounds like. It is published only as anonymous counts, never with my name. I can withdraw it any time from "My experiments".
api.need16: The open dataset is for people 16 or older.
api.hidden: Not enough voices here yet — be one of the first five.
api.share.open: This link is kept on research.daxfoundation.org. Open it? Your browser will contact that server.
api.share.closed: This link needs the research server, which isn't open yet.
api.added: Added. You can withdraw it any time.
open.hold: Hold the heart if you're 13 or older
